Menu Products Apps for teams Productivity Now Sales Soon Contracts Now Mastery Soon Agents and automations Automations Credits Agents Credits Apps for everyone Comms Included QR Included Analytics Soon Forms Soon Pricing About Learn Automation Project Management Marketing Forms Contracts CRM All articles Contact Login Mattering Automations connector A Gumroad MCP that is honest about the fifteen nodes that touch real customers 81 nodes on Gumroad's v2 API: products and variants, sales and refunds, license keys, discount codes, audience emails and workflows, the media library, payouts, earnings and tax forms. Fifteen of them are flagged destructive, and five of those delete nothing at all. They are flagged because a refund moves real money to a real customer, a published email reaches an audience with no recall, and a rotated license key stops working on the machine it was already installed on. 81 ready-made nodes One credential to connect Works with Claude, ChatGPT, and Matter Start free Browse the nodes What the Gumroad MCP connector does The Gumroad connector for Mattering Automations is 81 nodes on Gumroad's v2 API at api.gumroad.com, covering every operation Gumroad documents. Thirty three read and forty eight act. Products, variant categories and variants cover the catalogue. Sales, refunds, receipts, shipping and access revocation cover an order after it is placed. License keys cover software delivery, with enable, disable, rotate, seat decrement and a verify node that needs no credential at all. Offer codes, custom checkout fields, covers, thumbnails and the refund policy cover the storefront. Audience emails and workflows cover the mailing list. Payouts, annual earnings and tax forms cover the money coming back out. The media library and the four step file attachment flow cover assets. Every capability is a node on the Automations canvas, and every node speaks MCP, the open protocol for connecting AI assistants to tools. Claude, ChatGPT, and any MCP-capable assistant can use them, alongside Matter, the AI assistant built into the platform. So an assistant can read a week of sales with Gumroad: List Sales, spot the refund requests, and stop there while a person decides whether any money moves. Gumroad has no subscription plans, which makes the usual question on a page like this unusually simple to answer. There is no Pro tier, no Business tier and no monthly bill, so there is no plan for API access to sit behind. Gumroad's published pricing is a per-transaction cut and nothing else: 10 percent plus 50 cents on sales through your own profile and direct links, and 30 percent when a new customer finds you through Gumroad's Discover marketplace. Any account can create an application, generate an access token and call the API immediately. Nothing on this page is gated behind an upgrade, and there is no free tier exclusion list to read, because there is no paid tier to be excluded from. Fifteen nodes carry a destructive flag and it is worth reading which ones and why, because the flag is not only about deletion. Ten of them delete: a product, a variant, a whole variant category, an offer code, a custom checkout field, an audience email, a media file, a product cover, a product thumbnail or a webhook subscription. Gumroad documents no undelete for any of them and this API has no restore endpoint, so a workflow cannot put any of them back. The other five delete nothing and are flagged because of what they do to a person. Gumroad: Refund Sale moves money out of the seller's balance and back onto a real customer's card, and there is no unrefund endpoint anywhere on this API. Gumroad: Send Email publishes a draft to its audience, potentially every customer and follower the account has, with no recall. Gumroad: Rotate License Key issues a new key and invalidates the old one, so whatever the customer already installed stops validating and only that node's response will ever tell you the replacement. Gumroad: Disable License stops a customer's software validating on its next check-in. Gumroad: Revoke Sale Access takes a paying customer's library and downloads away without refunding them. Two more nodes reach a customer without being flagged, and both say so in their own descriptions. Gumroad: Resend Sale Receipt puts a real email in a buyer's inbox. Gumroad: Mark Sale As Shipped tells the buyer their order is on its way and shows them the tracking link, with no documented way to unmark it. And two workflow nodes can turn an edit into a send: on a published workflow whose send to past customers option is on, Gumroad: Add Workflow Email schedules the new step for eligible past customers, so a step added to a year old onboarding sequence can go out to everyone who ever bought, and Gumroad: Update Workflow Email can reschedule people already partway through when the delay changes. There is no idempotency mechanism on this API. Nothing accepts an idempotency key, so a retried create makes a second product, a retried send delivers the campaign twice, and a retried refund issues a second refund. Every node that creates something says so in its own description, and the practical consequence is that retry logic belongs on your side of the wire: guard a money-moving or audience-reaching step with a condition, a data table lookup or an approval rather than a retry policy. Two mechanical details shape how Gumroad workflows have to be built. Pagination is an opaque cursor: paginated listers return a next page key and accept it back, and there is no page number, no offset and no page size parameter anywhere on this API, so a workflow cannot jump to page seven and cannot ask for five hundred rows. Two endpoints break that pattern in useful ways and the nodes say which: Gumroad: List Product Subscribers returns everything by default and only paginates on request, capped at 100, and Gumroad: List Product Reviews returns up to 100 per page with no way to change it. Separately, responses from the v2 API are enveloped with a success flag, and a rejected request can answer HTTP 200 with success set to false and a message explaining why. The connector reads that flag rather than trusting the status, marks the node result unsuccessful when it is false, and lifts the message into the result as an error message so a workflow can branch on it without digging through the payload. The money handling deserves its own warning, because the failure is silent. Every money column on a Gumroad sale, including price, the Gumroad fee, tax, shipping, tips and variant price, is expressed in the minor units of that row's own currency, and the currency lives on the row rather than on the account. So a window of sales can mix currencies, and totalling the price column across it is wrong for the exchange rate in the obvious way and wrong by a factor of a hundred in a way nobody notices, because Gumroad documents that Japanese yen has no minor units at all. That is why the connector declares only quantity as safely aggregatable on the sales node. It is unitless, so it is the one column that can be summed across a mixed currency window without being quietly incorrect. Gumroad does not publish an MCP server of its own. Its first-party AI-facing tool is a command line interface that wraps the API and that Gumroad describes as built for humans and AI agents alike, rather than a Model Context Protocol server, and there is none in Gumroad's open source codebase or anywhere else it publishes. Community MCP servers for Gumroad do exist, built by independent developers rather than by Gumroad. So there is no vendor server to weigh against this connector, and the practical way to put Gumroad behind an MCP-capable assistant today is a connector like this one: nodes that also run on a schedule with nobody present, chain with every other connector in one workflow, hold the access token once in a shared workspace store rather than in each person's local config, and carry a destructive flag on the fifteen that need one. One connection, three surfaces Visual automations. Drag Gumroad nodes onto the canvas and wire them to triggers, conditions, and other apps. AI agents, yours or ours. These nodes speak MCP, the open protocol, so Claude, ChatGPT, and any MCP-capable assistant can use them, and Matter, the agent built into the platform, uses them natively. The whole platform. Combine with native tasks, projects, and other connectors, no middleware in between. Every Gumroad node, ready to drop on the canvas 81 nodes, generated from the connector itself so this list always matches what ships. Expand a category to browse. Read and query nodes 33 Gumroad: Download Tax Form Download the PDF of one tax form. This is the ONLY endpoint on the Gumroad API that does not return JSON on success: it answers with the raw PDF bytes and a Content-Disposition attachment header, and only switches to a JSON error envelope when it fails. This node therefore returns the file's metadata and its bytes base64 encoded rather than a parsed object, so it can be written to storage or attached to an email by a following node. Anything larger than 8 MB comes back as metadata only, because a very large base64 blob would bloat every downstream node input. The document contains the seller's tax identity, so treat the output as sensitive. US only, tax centre enabled, and requires the view_tax_data scope. Gumroad: Get Annual Earnings Fetch the annual earnings breakdown that matches the totals in Gumroad's own Tax Center: gross, fees, taxes, affiliate credit and net, all in the smallest currency unit, for one tax year. FULLY REFUNDED SALES ARE EXCLUDED from every aggregate, so this will not equal a naive sum of the sales list, and that is correct rather than a discrepancy. US only, tax centre enabled. A year outside the seller's available range, which runs from the account creation year to last year, returns 404. Requires the view_tax_data scope. Gumroad: Get Email Fetch one audience email in full: subject, HTML body, audience type, state, publish and schedule times, and its recipient and audience counts. Requires edit_emails or account. Gumroad: Get Offer Code Fetch one discount code by id, with its coupon text, its discount and how many times it has been redeemed. As with the lister, a fixed amount code carries amount_cents and a percentage code carries percent_off. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Get Payout Fetch one payout, optionally with the sale ids it covers and with a full transaction ledger matching the exported payout CSV. The transaction list is the useful part for reconciliation: each entry carries a type, date, purchase id, item and buyer, taxes, shipping, sale price, Gumroad fees and net total, and the types include Sale, Chargeback, Full Refund, Partial Refund, the PayPal and Stripe Connect refund and affiliate variants, and the payout transfers themselves. Note that transactions are OFF by default while sales are ON. Requires the view_payouts scope. Gumroad: Get Product Fetch one product in full. This returns everything the lister returns plus custom_html, the custom landing page, so it is the read half of the custom landing page workflow. It is also the only place to see a product's covers and attached files. Note that each attached file comes back as a TIME LIMITED SIGNED download URL rather than the canonical file URL, and the canonical URL cannot be recovered from a read, so a workflow that attaches files must keep the URL that Gumroad: Complete File Upload gave it. Requires view_profile, edit_products or account. Gumroad: Get Profile Custom HTML Read the seller's custom profile landing page: the stored source HTML, the rendered HTML, whether a landing page is in effect and the public profile URL. Gumroad keeps only the latest version with no history, so this node plus your own version control is the whole backup story for that page. Gumroad: Get Public Product Page Read the public display data for ANY Gumroad product page, with no credential at all. This is the read counterpart to the authenticated product nodes: it returns exactly what the rendered page shows, meaning price, covers, description, variants, ratings and the refund policy, and it never exposes buyer, seller private or analytics fields. Because it needs no token it works against products you do not own, which makes it the node for competitor and catalogue monitoring. Note the response has NO success key: it is a bare object with an api_version, so branch on the HTTP status rather than on success. Gumroad: Get Public Profile Read any creator's public profile with no credential: display name, bio, avatar, social links and the products shown in their public profile sections. Seller private fields such as email, balance and tax information are never included. Like the public product page, the response has NO success key, so branch on the HTTP status. Gumroad: Get Refund Policy Read the account level refund policy: the period, the display title derived from it, the fine print and whether it is IN EFFECT. Read in_effect before writing anything, because it decides which of two mutually exclusive systems is live: when it is true the account policy governs and per product refund_period values are refused, and when it is false the product level fields govern and updating this policy is refused. Gumroad: Get Sale Fetch one sale in full. The detail shape is RICHER than the lister's and the extra fields are the ones a finance workflow actually needs: tip_cents, the tax label and whether tax was included, the payment processor and its transaction id and fee, the buyer's review, and a buyer_presentment block giving what the customer was actually charged in their own currency with the FX rate used. Requires view_sales. Gumroad: Get Subscriber Fetch one subscriber by id, with their product, email, purchase ids, recurrence, license key and the cancellation, end and failure timestamps that decide whether the subscription is still alive. Note the response key is the plural subscribers even though it holds a single object, which is a Gumroad quirk rather than a typo here. Requires view_sales. Gumroad: Get User Fetch the authenticated seller's own account: name, bio, user id, profile picture and profile URL. Two conditional fields worth knowing about because their absence is not an error: email only appears for a token holding view_sales, and url only appears once a username is set. This is also the cheapest way to confirm a credential works, which is what the connector's auth test uses. Gumroad: Get Variant Fetch one variant by id: its name, its price difference in the smallest currency unit and its purchase cap. Requires view_profile, edit_products or account. Gumroad: Get Variant Category Fetch one variant category by id. The category record itself is just an id and a title; to see the options inside it use Gumroad: List Variants. Requires view_profile, edit_products or account. Gumroad: Get Workflow Fetch one active workflow with every email step in it and each step's delivery statistics: sent count, opens, open rate, clicks and click rate. This is the only place the step ids appear, so run it before editing a step. Requires edit_emails or account. Gumroad: List Categories Fetch Gumroad's full product category tree, flat, with each entry's id, name, human label, full path and parent id. This is the lookup behind the category field on product create and update: Gumroad wants the PATH, for example design/ui-and-web/figma, not the label. It is also the source for the category picker on both product write nodes, so run it once and the pickers fill themselves. Gumroad: List Custom Fields List the extra questions a product asks a buyer at checkout, each with its name and whether it is required. The name is the identifier as well as the label, so this is the node to run before updating or deleting one. Note the shape quirk: required comes back as the STRING false rather than a boolean. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: List Emails List the seller's audience emails with their state, audience type, schedule and recipient counts. Filter with type to see only published, scheduled or draft. This is the source for every email picker in this connector, and the node to run first when auditing what is queued to go out. Requires edit_emails or account. Gumroad: List Media Files List the images in the account's media library, newest first, with each file's id, name, extension, size, hosted URL and status. The library exists because custom product and profile pages render under a Content Security Policy that BLOCKS images loaded from other sites: only inline data images and Gumroad's own asset hosts are allowed, so an image hosted anywhere else simply will not appear. Upload it here first and embed the URL this returns. Files belong to the account rather than to one product, so the same image can be reused everywhere. Requires view_profile specifically: this is the endpoint family Gumroad names when it says an account only token is refused. Gumroad: List Offer Codes List a product's discount codes with how many times each has been used. The response shape varies per row and that is the thing to wire around: a fixed amount code carries amount_cents and a percentage code carries percent_off, never both, so read whichever is present rather than assuming one. A universal code is one that applies to every product on the account, and those appear here too. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: List Payouts List the seller's payouts with amount, currency, status, creation and processing timestamps, the processor used and a masked bank account or PayPal address. Statuses seen here include payable, pending, completed and failed. One row can be unlike the others: the upcoming payout is included by default and carries a NULL id, because it has not happened yet, so any workflow keying on id has to handle that or turn include_upcoming off. Requires the view_payouts scope. Gumroad: List Product Reviews List the reviews shown on one of your product pages, newest first, with the rating, the buyer's message, the purchase id and your own published response if you left one. Only PUBLICLY VISIBLE reviews are returned, meaning a buyer left a written message or an approved video: a star only rating with no message still counts towards the product's average_rating but never appears here, so the row count and the review count on the product page will not agree. Up to 100 per page. Available with any read scope. Gumroad: List Product Subscribers List the ACTIVE subscribers to one membership or subscription product, with each one's email, purchase ids, recurrence, license key and lifecycle timestamps. Reading the state is the part that catches people out: a subscription is TERMINATED if any of failed_at, ended_at or cancelled_at is set and in the past, so those three have to be checked together rather than trusting one. The status field is one of alive, payment_method_update_required, pending_cancellation, pending_failure, failed_payment, fixed_subscription_period_ended or cancelled. Pagination is opt in here, unlike the rest of this API: without paginated the endpoint returns everything, and with it the page is capped at 100. Requires view_sales. Gumroad: List Products List every product on the authenticated seller's account, with price, currency, publication state, tags, category, thumbnail and the whole variant tree for tiered memberships. This is the node most Gumroad workflows start from, and it is the source for every product picker in this connector. Two shape notes worth knowing before wiring to it: url is documented as deprecated and always null, so read short_url instead, and sales_count and sales_usd_cents only appear when the token holds view_sales or account. The list shape also differs from the single-product shape, which adds custom_html. Requires view_profile, edit_products or account. Gumroad: List Resource Subscriptions List the account's active webhook subscriptions FOR ONE RESOURCE. The resource name is required, so there is no way to see every subscription in a single call: to audit them all, run this once per resource across the eight supported names. Each row carries the subscription id needed to remove it. Gumroad: List Sales List the seller's successful sales, filterable by date range, product, buyer email, order id, customer name or license key. Each row is a full purchase record: price and fee in the smallest unit of the SALE'S OWN currency, buyer email, variants chosen, answers to custom fields, UTM parameters, subscription state, affiliate credit and any license key. The window is after and before as YYYY-MM-DD dates, and pagination is the opaque next_page_key cursor with no page size to tune. The currency is per row rather than per account, which matters before adding any of these numbers up. Requires view_sales. Gumroad: List Tax Forms List the tax forms Gumroad has generated for the seller, currently 1099-K and 1099-MISC, each with its year, type and filing timestamp. A null filed_at means the form exists but has not been filed yet. This is US ONLY and only for sellers with the tax centre enabled, so an account outside that will get nothing back rather than an explanation. Asking for a year outside the seller's available range, which runs from the account creation year to last year, returns 404. Requires the view_tax_data scope. Gumroad: List Upcoming Payouts Fetch the payouts that have not been paid yet. There can be at most two at any moment. Every row has a NULL id and a payable status because these have not happened, so the amounts are forecasts that can still move as sales, refunds and chargebacks land: do not store them as though they were settled figures. Requires the view_payouts scope. Gumroad: List Variant Categories List a product's variant categories. A category is the GROUPING, for example Colors or Tier, and the individual options inside it are variants. For a tiered membership the category is usually the single Tier group and each membership tier is a variant. This is the source for every variant category picker in this connector. Requires view_profile, edit_products or account. Gumroad: List Variants List the options inside one variant category, with each one's name, price difference in the smallest currency unit and purchase cap. This is the source for every variant picker in this connector, and it needs both the product and the category first because a variant only means something inside its own category. Requires view_profile, edit_products or account. Gumroad: List Workflows List the seller's ACTIVE workflows, newest first, with each one's audience type, trigger, product, state, step count and audience filters. Only active workflows are returned, so this is not a complete inventory of everything ever built. It is the source for the workflow picker on the two workflow email nodes. Requires edit_emails or account. Gumroad: Verify License Check whether a license key is valid for a product, and get back the purchase behind it: buyer email, price, quantity, subscription state, refund and dispute flags, and the number of times the key has been used. This is the ONE endpoint on the whole Gumroad API that needs no credential and no OAuth application at all, which is why it can run from a customer's own machine. Watch increment_uses_count: it DEFAULTS TO TRUE, so every plain check burns a seat on a multi seat license. Set it off for a read only check such as a dashboard poll. Read the refunded, disputed and subscription_ended_at fields as well as the success flag, because a valid key can belong to a refunded purchase. Action nodes 48 Gumroad: Abort File Upload Cancel a multipart upload that failed partway through, so the half uploaded parts are not left behind. Read the status field in the response, because it has two meanings and only one of them is final: accepted means S3 took the cancellation but parts still in flight may land seconds later, and already_gone means there is no multipart session for this upload_id. Call this again while you see accepted, and stop when you see already gone. Requires edit_products. Gumroad: Add Product Cover Add a cover to a product from a publicly reachable URL. Gumroad FETCHES the URL server side and stores its own copy, so the URL has to be reachable over HTTP or HTTPS from the public internet: a private link or a presigned upload URL will not work. Images in JPEG, PNG and GIF are accepted, and so are video URLs including YouTube and Vimeo, which come back as an oembed cover. This is a PUBLICLY VISIBLE change: the cover appears on the product page as soon as it is stored. The response returns the full cover list and the main_cover_id; reorder them with the cover_ids field on Gumroad: Update Product. Gumroad has no idempotency mechanism, so running this node twice creates two records. Guard retries on your side. Requires edit_products. Gumroad: Add Workflow Email Add one email step to an existing workflow, without changing whether the workflow is published. The new step inherits the workflow's state, and that is the part that reaches people: on a PUBLISHED workflow whose send_to_past_customers is true, adding a step SCHEDULES IT FOR ELIGIBLE PAST CUSTOMERS, so a step added to a year old onboarding sequence can go out to everyone who ever bought. Check the workflow's state and that flag first. Abandoned cart workflows do not accept added steps at all. Gumroad has no idempotency mechanism, so running this node twice creates two records. Guard retries on your side. Requires edit_emails or account. Gumroad: Complete File Upload Step 3 of 4: finalize the multipart upload started by Gumroad: Presign File Upload by submitting the ETag of every part. The S3 object is not usable until this succeeds. The returned file_url is the CANONICAL url and the only value that can be attached to a product, so store it: reading the product back later gives a time limited signed URL instead and the canonical one cannot be recovered from a read. Step 4 is passing that URL to Gumroad: Create Product or Gumroad: Update Product. Requires edit_products. Gumroad: Create Custom Field Add an extra question to a product's checkout, for example a phone number or a Twitter handle. A PUBLICLY VISIBLE change: the field appears at checkout immediately, and marking it required means a buyer cannot complete a purchase without answering. Whatever buyers enter is returned on the sale record under custom_fields, so only ask for what you need. The name doubles as the identifier for later updates and deletes. Gumroad has no idempotency mechanism, so running this node twice creates two records. Guard retries on your side. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Create Email Create an audience email. By default it is a DRAFT and nothing is sent, which is the safe way to use this node. Setting publish to true, or draft to false, SENDS IT IMMEDIATELY to the chosen audience, which can be every follower and customer the seller has, and there is no recall. Scheduling is a separate step on an existing email rather than an option here. Gumroad has no idempotency mechanism, so running this node twice creates two records. Guard retries on your side. A retried run with publish on sends the campaign twice. Requires edit_emails or account. Gumroad: Create Offer Code Create a discount code. name is the text a buyer types at checkout, so it becomes usable the moment this succeeds and anyone who learns it can redeem it: treat a generated code as live money off. amount_off is read together with offer_type, which defaults to cents, so 100 with the default means one dollar off in USD while 100 with percent means free. Set universal to apply it to EVERY product on the account rather than only this one. Cap the blast radius with max_purchase_count. Gumroad has no idempotency mechanism, so running this node twice creates two records. Guard retries on your side. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Create Product Create a product as a DRAFT. It is not visible to buyers until Gumroad: Enable Product publishes it, which makes this the safe half of a two-step publish. native_type is fixed at creation and can never be changed afterwards, so choose it deliberately. Prices are in the smallest unit of the currency, so 100 means one dollar in USD. Covers and thumbnails are attached separately, and files need the four-call upload flow first. Gumroad has no idempotency mechanism, so running this node twice creates two records. Guard retries on your side. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Create Resource Subscription Subscribe a URL of yours to one kind of Gumroad event, so Gumroad POSTs to it whenever that event happens. This MANAGES GUMROAD'S OWN WEBHOOKS and is not a Mattering trigger: the endpoint you name has to exist and be reachable before this is useful. Eight resources are supported: sale, refund, dispute, dispute_won, cancellation, subscription_updated, subscription_ended and subscription_restarted. The sale, refund, dispute and dispute_won payloads follow Gumroad's Ping format; the four subscription payloads carry subscription_id, product_id, product_name, user_id, user_email and purchase_ids plus their own fields. Subscribing to sales requires the view_sales scope specifically. Gumroad has no idempotency mechanism, so running this node twice creates two records. Guard retries on your side. Gumroad: Create Variant Add one option to a variant category, for example Red inside Colors, or Premium inside Tier. A PUBLICLY VISIBLE change: the option appears in the chooser on the product page immediately and can be bought. price_difference_cents is a DIFFERENCE from the base price, in the smallest currency unit, not an absolute price, so 250 adds 2.50 on top in a currency with minor units. Gumroad has no idempotency mechanism, so running this node twice creates two records. Guard retries on your side. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Create Variant Category Create a variant category on a product, which is the group buyers choose from at checkout, for example Colors or Format. The category on its own does nothing until it has options: add those with Gumroad: Create Variant. A PUBLICLY VISIBLE change once options exist, because it adds a chooser to the product page. Gumroad has no idempotency mechanism, so running this node twice creates two records. Guard retries on your side. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Decrement License Uses Count Give a seat back on a multi seat license by lowering its uses count by one. This is the deactivate half of a seat management flow: when a customer uninstalls on one machine, call this so they can activate on another without buying more seats. It pairs with the increment that Gumroad: Verify License performs by default. Gumroad: Delete Custom Field PERMANENTLY delete a checkout question. It disappears from the product's checkout immediately and Gumroad documents no undelete. Answers already captured on past sales are part of those sale records rather than of this field, so removing the question stops collecting new answers rather than erasing old ones. The field is addressed by its name in the URL and a name with spaces is percent encoded for you. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Delete Email PERMANENTLY delete an audience email, draft or published. Gumroad documents no undelete, so the copy is gone. Deleting a published email does not unsend it: the messages already delivered stay in recipients' inboxes, and a published email can also have a public page on the seller's profile, which this removes. Requires edit_emails or account. Gumroad: Delete Media File Delete a file from the media library. The file leaves the library immediately and the hosted copy is queued for removal, so ANY PAGE STILL EMBEDDING ITS URL will show a broken image once the purge runs. Because media files are account wide rather than per product, that can be several product pages and the profile at once, and nothing in the API tells you which. Not reversible: restoring means uploading the original again, which produces a new id and a new URL. Requires edit_profile specifically. Gumroad: Delete Offer Code PERMANENTLY delete a discount code. The code stops working at checkout immediately, so anyone who has been given it and has not yet redeemed it will be turned away: check times_used against what you expected before running this in a campaign teardown. Gumroad documents no undelete. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Delete Product PERMANENTLY delete a product. Gumroad documents no undelete and this API has no restore endpoint, so this is not recoverable from a workflow. Existing buyers, their sales records and their library access are outside what this call promises to preserve, so treat it as an operator action rather than an automated one. If the goal is only to stop selling, use Gumroad: Disable Product, which takes the product off sale and is reversible. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Delete Product Cover Remove a cover from a product. A PUBLICLY VISIBLE change that takes effect on the product page immediately, and it is not reversible from this API: Gumroad stores its own copy of the image and deleting the cover discards it, so restoring means adding the original source URL again. The response returns the remaining covers and the new main_cover_id, which is null once the last cover is gone. Requires edit_products. Gumroad: Delete Product Thumbnail Remove a product's thumbnail so it falls back to Gumroad's default. A PUBLICLY VISIBLE change, live immediately, and not reversible from this API: the stored image is discarded, so restoring means setting it again from the original source. Requires edit_products. Gumroad: Delete Resource Subscription Unsubscribe from a Gumroad event, so it stops POSTing to your endpoint. The events themselves keep happening, they just stop being delivered, and Gumroad does not replay what was missed while a subscription was gone: anything that occurs between this call and a re-subscribe is simply not delivered. Re-subscribing creates a new subscription with a new id. Gumroad: Delete Variant PERMANENTLY delete one option from a variant category. A PUBLICLY VISIBLE change: the option disappears from the product page and can no longer be bought. Gumroad documents no undelete, and on a tiered membership the variant IS a tier, so removing one affects the members on it. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Delete Variant Category PERMANENTLY delete a variant category. This removes the whole chooser from the product page, and the variants inside it go with it, so this is much larger than deleting one option. Gumroad documents no undelete. On a tiered membership the category IS the tier structure, so removing it changes what existing members are on: do not run this against a live membership from an automation. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Disable License Disable a license key. CUSTOMER FACING and immediate: whatever the customer installed stops validating the next time it checks in, so this is how a paying customer's software goes dark. It is the right call for a chargeback or a leaked key and the wrong call to automate on a hunch. Reversible with Gumroad: Enable License, though the customer will have noticed. Gumroad: Disable Product Unpublish a product so it stops selling. A PUBLICLY VISIBLE change: the product page stops taking orders and the product leaves the seller's public listing. Nothing is deleted and existing buyers keep what they bought, so this is the reversible way to stop selling something. Reverse it with Gumroad: Enable Product. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Enable License Re-enable a license key that was disabled, so the customer's software starts validating again. CUSTOMER FACING in the good direction: whatever they installed begins working the next time it checks in. The reverse of Gumroad: Disable License. Gumroad: Enable Product Publish a product so it is on sale and visible to buyers. This is the second half of the create then publish flow, and it is a PUBLICLY VISIBLE change: the product page goes live, the product can appear on the seller's profile, and anyone with the link can buy. Reversible with Gumroad: Disable Product. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Mark Sale As Shipped Mark a physical product's sale as shipped, optionally with a tracking URL. This is CUSTOMER FACING: Gumroad tells the buyer their order is on its way and shows them the tracking link, so running it early tells someone their parcel has gone when it has not. There is no documented way to unmark it. Requires the mark_sales_as_shipped scope specifically, which exists so a fulfilment integration does not need refund rights. Gumroad: Presign File Upload Step 1 of 4 in attaching a file to a product: start a multipart upload and get back an upload_id, a key, the canonical file_url and one presigned URL per 100 MB part. Step 2 is NOT a Gumroad call and has no node here: PUT each part's raw bytes to its own presigned URL with the generic HTTP node or a worker, and keep the ETag response header from each. Then use Gumroad: Complete File Upload, or Gumroad: Abort File Upload if it goes wrong. The presigned URLs EXPIRE AFTER 900 SECONDS, so a workflow that presigns and then waits on a human will fail.
